1|417.61273342795715|93.6796259999999|526.8036609999997|X-ray quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) are rare and enigmatic phenomena that increasingly show a connection
1|405.2929162500001|84.7425137999999|526.9723651999996|to tidal disruption events (TDEs). However, the recently discovered QPEs in ZTF19acnskyy ("Ansky") appear
1|392.9236786935482|84.7425137999999|526.7033749999995|to be linked to an active galactic nucleus (AGN) rather than a TDE, as their slow decay and AGN-like variability
1|380.4122944977273|84.8819901999999|526.6535619999994|differ markedly from that of typical TDEs. This finding may imply broader formation channels for QPEs. To
1|367.85855255714296|84.8122519999999|526.4044969999994|further investigate Ansky’s nature, we obtained a timely ultraviolet (UV) spectrum, which reveals a featureless,
1|355.5059343880437|84.7823641999999|526.8627765999992|TDE-like spectrum devoid of broad optical or UV emission lines. Additionally, the steep UV continuum, fitted
1|342.9887365469881|84.6428877999999|526.9723651999992|by a power-law with an index of -2.6, aligns more closely with TDEs than with AGNs. Compared to other
1|330.7055569836957|84.8122519999999|526.9725115999998|featureless TDEs, Ansky exhibits a significantly lower blackbody luminosity (∼ 1043 erg s−1 ) and much longer
1|318.09530696354176|84.66281299999983|527.0022529999992|rise/decay timescales, suggesting a distinct TDE subclass. An offset TDE involving an intermediate-mass black
1|305.61153705833345|84.70266339999984|526.7571730399993|hole is unlikely, given its position consistent with the galactic center with a 3σ upper limit of 54 pc. Instead, we
1|293.0597147787235|84.66281299999983|526.7531879999993|propose that Ansky may result from the tidal disruption of a post-main-sequence star by a typical supermassive
1|280.74087482903275|84.64288779999983|526.8030009999994|black hole. Our findings strengthen the growing evidence for TDE-QPE associations, although other formation
1|268.31070596153864|84.86206499999983|380.33285579999966|channels for QPEs remain plausible and await future observational efforts.

20|402.8442723267239|72.075052|430.0283261735998|It is hard to imagine the world before the Internet. A generation of digital natives has
20|389.71413496508654|71.9756279033241|430.2337351402999|grown up with ubiquitous connectivity, where neither borders nor language seems a
20|376.87892223406976|71.73433259999999|430.08334578279994|barrier to communication.1 And yet less than 20 years ago the global information en-
20|363.82446209272996|71.72796629999999|430.0936992399|vironment was a much more controlled and regulated space, organized around sover-
20|350.8937350302752|72.05971939999999|430.11106696299976|eign states. Throughout much of modern history, governments have wrestled with the
20|338.12406023147037|71.97005639999999|430.23638893809994|tensions of the relentless drive to build new technologies and the unpredictable and
20|325.0014890948644|72.05971939999999|430.1011950666999|often counterproductive consequences that ﬂow from them for their power and au-
20|312.2213088240914|71.97005639999999|430.04733825969987|thority.2 No less of a historical ﬁgure than Stalin captured this tension between the
20|299.06681906270677|72.05851940000001|430.21733703480015|quest for modernity and the compulsion to control. When presented with a proposal
20|286.3164540267011|71.9688564|430.0567864669998|to build a modern telephone system for the new Soviet state he reportedly replied ‘‘I
20|273.2851070679462|72.05851940000001|360.85350225679974|can imagine no greater instrument of counterrevolution in our time.’’
20|260.4077438618977|80.6931526|430.06508589780003|The rise of the Internet coincided with a major set of political upheavals that culmi-
20|247.46298335599468|71.98678900000002|430.20869352159986|nated with the collapse of the Soviet Union and communist bloc. In the euphoria that
20|234.4719064779623|72.05851940000001|430.3421634320852|ensued the idea of technological redemption inevitable democratization and for
20|221.3292024793698|72.18404760000001|430.37888286189985|some, the end of history, coalesced into a popular ideology that equated technology
20|208.48332983683582|71.76263150000001|430.11889602709977|with empowerment. This idea was far from new. Indeed the telegraph electrical light-
20|195.5603675496943|71.98678900000002|430.07381347070003|ing and telephony all emerged at similarly transformational historical junctures lead-
20|182.4772378692106|71.98678900000002|430.12755747289987|ing to a long pedigree of speculation regarding the democratizing role of technology in
20|156.79692467776215|80.6917326|430.1081925436|There is no doubt that the Internet has unleashed a wide-ranging and globally signif-
20|143.8804605232868|71.985759|430.02896695585974|icant shift in communications—a shift that has led to the empowerment of individuals
20|130.71122773664624|72.075422|430.05533505089994|and nonstate actors on an unprecedented scale. At times, the Internet seems uncon-
20|117.7432455103738|71.96782639999999|430.4137449607998|trollable, a constantly evolving and dynamic virtual realm, reshaped continuously by
20|104.81259751985856|72.075422|430.0104228542|a growing number of users at edge points of the network. But Newtonian physics is as
20|91.87055276273041|71.985759|430.01856425459977|relevant in politics and cyberspace as it is in the physical realm. Just as with previous
20|78.91036711565036|71.96782639999999|430.15417057579987|technological developments, as the Internet has grown in political signiﬁcance, an
21|572.0653199307483|73.94615200000001|431.90804816767985|architecture of control—through technology, regulation, norms, and political calculus
21|559.0895884232141|73.982031|348.66438134023|—has emerged to shape a new geopolitical information landscape.
21|546.4295722185985|82.95709300000001|431.9791648740001|In 2008 the OpenNet Initiative (ONI) published its ﬁrst global study—Access Denied:
21|533.4221820864395|74.21508200000001|431.9732849235201|The Practice and Policy of Global Internet Filtering4—which documented how states are
21|520.3398183885852|74.0562476|432.1167856204999|seeking to establish borders in cyberspace. Our snapshot of 41 countries discovered
21|507.29620053593754|73.8410564|432.1170187442999|that states were busy constructing defensive perimeters to deny access to unwanted

21|468.53761234335127|73.85898900000001|431.97302355282|ﬁltering systems at the backbone of the country’s Internet—popularly known as the
21|455.73438027887136|74.09211280000001|432.24924592560524|‘‘Great Firewall of China’’—and it has become a paradigm of Internet censorship ever
21|442.7183816653401|74.0562476|432.526934895559|since. ‘‘Chinese-style’’ ﬁltering—as we call it here—represents the ﬁrst generation of
21|416.7525182171167|82.95978199999998|432.22363398291503|In Chinese-style ﬁltering lists of Internet protocol (IP) addresses keywords and/or
21|403.6903847361119|73.93051939999997|432.2693534399001|domains are programmed into routers or software packages that are situated at key
21|390.65425388221365|73.94845199999997|431.99126364539995|Internet choke points, typically at international gateways or among major Internet ser-
21|377.9073324953651|73.59876629999997|431.97327093260003|vice providers (ISPs).5 Requests that are made for any information contained in the

21|339.0106088926625|73.949152|432.1530790900998|always static ﬁxed in time and relatively easy to discern using the methods developed
21|326.12326184195234|73.93121939999999|431.5608101436|over time by the OpenNet Initiative’s researchers (see box on ONI’s methodology).
21|313.07423022481845|73.74292709999999|392.8085332739997|Moreover, determined Internet users can circumvent them with relative ease.
21|300.27162960466495|82.7000693|432.08065507729987|Not all countries have been as forthright with their rationale for ﬁltering Internet

11|588.7303691176464|68.3169|419.2640991000004|Miranda Forsyth researched and wrote this book while teaching at the University
11|575.5009140624999|68.3829|419.13385270000003|of the South Pacific Law School in Vanuatu for the past six years. During this
11|562.3205540983606|68.2509|419.1837999999999|time, she acquired depth and breadth of knowledge of law and kastom in the
11|549.128191935484|68.50479999999997|419.3254579|South Pacific beyond Vanuatu from students who attended her classes from
11|535.9222499999995|68.28479999999998|420.100448|island societies all over the South Pacific. She also enjoys a broad network of
11|522.6563624999999|68.28479999999998|419.1597911999998|indigenous and non-indigenous friends in Vanuatu who are deep thinkers and
11|509.4625411764704|68.25179999999997|419.2426999999999|repositories of great learning about Melanesian kastom. All this combines with
11|496.3082014925372|68.25169999999994|419.1408264999999|the sharpness of Miranda Forsyth’s intellect to equip her to write an ambitious
11|465.51785781249964|68.47169999999994|419.2341124999997|One thing that impresses about the book is the wide-angle lens through which
11|452.105846153846|68.28469999999994|419.17595849999964|it views not just one island or language group ofVanuatu, but the whole, broad
11|439.05566268656713|68.63669999999995|419.2725515999998|diversity and patterns of Vanuatu kastom and how that plurality interacts with
11|425.87062380952364|68.25159999999991|419.1365317999996|the entire national criminal justice system of Vanuatu. That ambition has
11|412.610319117647|68.63659999999992|418.9809068999999|demanded impressively extensive fieldwork. There is no more important calling
11|399.48108235294103|68.27359999999992|419.2612435999998|for social scientists born in Australia, like Miranda Forsyth, than to document
11|386.3603428571426|68.31759999999991|418.6951049999999|and draw out the implications ofthe diversity ofthe cultures ofthe South Pacific.
11|373.06303880597|68.30659999999992|418.61274849999967|No part of the world has more linguistic and cultural plurality than Melanesia.
11|359.7409676470586|68.33959999999992|418.9828342999997|As geographical mobility increases, almost everywhere in the world is becoming
11|346.6060230769227|68.31759999999991|419.1753843999997|more culturally diverse than it used to be. At the same time, everywhere in the
11|333.41488115942|68.32859999999991|419.19540969999974|world is caught up in certain homogenising influences of globalisation. So there
11|320.1982377049177|68.28459999999991|419.13506199999983|is special merit in ANU E Press concentrating its admirably open-access
11|307.07388333333313|68.33959999999992|419.1473040999998|publishing on lessons from the most diverse part ofthe world on how it sustains
11|293.8565824561401|68.25159999999991|353.43789259999977|that diversity while coping with globalisation that homogenises.
11|276.2853579710139|68.42759999999991|419.1845152999997|There are few more globalised institutions than criminal justice. Until a couple
11|263.0486666666663|68.38359999999992|419.1622952999998|of centuries ago, very few societies had the distinction between criminal and
11|249.78650147058778|68.5155999999999|419.21828099999976|civil law that was invented in Europe. Today every nation in the world recognises
11|236.83439999999945|68.25159999999991|419.1543799999998|that distinction in its law. It was only in 1829 that Sir Robert Peel introduced
11|223.43860714285668|68.25159999999991|419.18060219999995|the organisational innovation of a paramilitary organisation dedicated to crime
11|210.39341194029808|68.5155999999999|419.2509332999998|control when he established the London Metropolitan Police. That institution
11|197.0689485294113|68.31759999999991|418.9888144999998|has utterly globalised. There is no city in the world one can visit without seeing
11|183.92876164383512|68.33959999999992|418.73634369999985|police in their almost invariably blue uniforms. Before Peel’s Metropolitan Police,
11|170.59178571428532|68.5155999999999|411.53942289999975|constables were generalist regulators of overwhelmingly civil law obligations.
12|616.0571739130434|79.6559|430.54798249999993|My own view is that the globalising Peelian revolution in policing was a desirable

49|229.4318879310344|58.491|343.84739999999994|restorative justice. The key value is that because injustice hurts,

49|108.09400206896548|58.57508000000001|344.02458|Empowerment means preventing the state from ‘stealing conflicts’3
